Food Security

By: Bernadette Maguire | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Malema says the land must be taken and Zuma must pay - we look at how the emotional proposals around land will impact on our food security.

Summary:
It seems whenever politicians want to win votes the land issue rears its head. Its a cheap shot at winning votes. EFF leader Julius Malema has been very vocal on the issue and it seems it has not gone unnoticed by the ruling party. President Zuma at the recent lekgothla promised to ramp up land expropriation and it appears his remarks have sent jitters through the agricultural sector. Landbou.com have 13000 farms for sale and commercial farmers have dwindled from 67 000 in 1990 to 33 000 currently. These are the same farmers who provide around 95% of our locally produced food.

Further information:
Commercial agriculture is worried. The land expropriation bill calls for no more than 2 title deeds and land not bigger than 12000 hectares. Given that this is a numbers game that relies on economies of scale a farm in the Western Cape cannot be compared to a farm in the Karoo for instance and organised agriculture says the plans are poorly thought out and unviable. Couple this with calls from government for farmers to hand over 50% of their farms to their workers in BEE deals and its easy to see why our food security is in danger.

And if that is not enough - if we don't get rain in the next 10 days Grain SA warns our crops for the season will be dismal.

We ask how do we keep our food basket full given all these dynamics?

Hy is baie gebalanseerd en nugter in sy seining. Verder kan jy vir Sakkie van Niekerk (083 294 8465) kontak wat in Kenhardt omgewing boer waar 'n ekonomiese eenheid afhangende van die plaas groter as 12 000 ha is. Dan ook vir George Barnard (082 322 7471) wat in Groblersdal boer wat oor verskeie titelaktes (heelwat meer as 2) beskik wat saam 'n ekonomiese eenheid uitmaak. Indien hy net op 2 titelaktes moet boer sal sy ekonomie van skaal sodanig negatief beinvloed word dat hy nie sal kan voortgaan nie.

Press Release:


Food Security
We have farmers to thank for the food on our tables. But South Africa has lost thousands of commercial farmers over the past 20 years and recent announcements around land reform have farmers feeling more insecure than ever. Carte Blanche asks: will new laws governing agricultural land put farmers out of business and less food on our tables?


Script:


Script Food Security

VO: 30
If you’ve eaten today chances are you have a farmer or two or three to thank. But in a worrying and growing trend our commercial farming base is being eroded and it’s threatening food security. Already we’ve seen the number of farmers drop from 65000 in 1990 to 36000 today.

That means we have nearly half the farmers. Groblersdal based, George Barnard who produces 15000 tonnes of staples every year and employs 250 labourers says it time government takes notice.

George:
The only thing we as commercial farmers want is for the government to realize the value that it has in commercial farmers, if you look all over the world you will see that we are close to the best if not the best farmers all over the world.

VO: 10”
The number of commercial farmers may even be eroded further – given the land reform sword hanging over their heads which organized agriculture says is to blame for a record 13000 farms on the market at the moment around the country.

George:
I don’t want to buy a piece of land and start developing it and putting effort in and then in a year or two’s time I might lose it because of land reform.

VO: 8”
These jitters in the market are largely due to government’s plans, announced at the legotla in January, to ramp up land reform.

Zuma:
We commit that the land will be returned to our people, the ANC calls on its government to act with the necessary speed to put the legistlation in place, this year to ensure that this happens.

Bongani link
There is no doubt that the land question is an emotive one, and its often used for political point scoring but in reality it’s a complex issue that needs well considered solutions.

VO: 10”
It’s hard for the ANC to ignore the land restitution issue when opposition politicians like EFF leader Julius Malema are baying for change and have been, for years.

Malema:
We expropriate from those who own the land and give it to the public and there must be a point where we say, look we have been talking, now we are taking.

VO: 11
But the problem with the current process is government is dragging its heels. Farmers like Gideon Marule claim land is being given to people with no real interest in farming.

Gideon:
Not land that is being given by public servants to their friends and tender entrepeneurs who give them kickbacks.

VO: 8”
If we follow the same model as Zimbabwe where land was doled out, some say for votes – Gideon reckons we may run the risk of having rows of empty shelves.

Gideon:
I see disaster coming, I see that we are going to be food insecure like Zimbabwe.

ADD VO: 6”
Tempers are starting to flare and last week farmers and ANC Secretary General Gwede Mantashe were at loggerheads over radical proposed reforms.

Bongani:
Are we looking at Zimbabwe as a possible model?

Gwede
That is not a model. It will be the irony of resisting change. That model will happen if change is resisted.
Bongani:
Is that a threat?

Gwede:
It’s not a threat, it’s a reality that will confront us.

VO: 12”
To appease supporters the president announced a raft of new policies and plans. Starting by sharing the land between workers and farmers as part of a 50/50 scheme. It’s been met with resistance.

George:
When you want to create wealth to somebody, you learn him to bake a cake, so that he can bake his own cake. You don’t take a cake and divide it in half because then you create proverty.

VO: 7”
George says he works on economies of scale and that splitting the farm will put his operation out of business.

George:
You know its basically the same as taking 50% of every person out there, 50% of their house, 50% of the value that you’ve got in stocks, this will also mean that this farming operation of mine is 50% smaller which will not make it viable anymore.

VO:
Bennie van Zyl, general manager for the biggest farming union, TAU, has come out criticizing the move.

Bennie:
Government have to go and rethink, what are they going doing? Are they trying to build a future or are they trying to re-address the history? And with that we are not going to take this country forward.


VO:
But the ANC sees it differently.

Bongani:
Will 50/50 become la

Gwede:
50/50 as a policy proposal is right in terms of saying: the message is, land must be shared among those who work it. And the second thing that is important is we must demystify this question of, black ownership of land is equal to destruction of productivity. That must be demystified.

VO: 14”
There are many problems to iron out – like how will farm workers secure working capital and how will they cope if their crops fail and they sit with debt and no income? It’s hard enough for emerging farmers who don’t have title deeds.

Bongani link:
One of the strongest criticisms of the land restitution process is that many of the beneficiaries are able to work the soil but don’t have title deeds. Its rather like giving someone a beautiful car but not the keys.

Bennie:
Now it is dead capital. If they hand out the title deeds to these new entrance farmers then it starts to be working capital. Then they can use it as collateral.

Gideon:
We as beneficiaries of land reform, having to be stifled and paralysed for years like myself…its heart breaking.

VO: 19”
The official ANC argument is that they don’t want emerging farmers to sell their properties and that they should be using their crops or livestock as surity for loans. Despite running a successful farm and proving his worth to Government ,Gideon has not been able to buy the farm he’s been leasing for 35 years.

Gideon:
I’m shivering…I know I can’t settlee. You know tenure insecurity is a terrible thing. I know I can be kicked out from this farm anytime.

VO: 15”
So why not reward people like Gideon who have shown commitment. By the same token the sector also wants to see an end to policies that punish farmers for being successful. Like the new ceiling they have put on land ownership.

Zuma:
In terms of our new proposed laws a ceiling on land ownership will be set at a maximum of 12000 hectares.

VO: 12”
While 12000 hectares would be huge and unmanageable in areas like the Western Cape – it’s a different story in the Northern Cape and Karoo where economically viable farm is much smaller.

Bennie:
If you look into the Northern Cape it rise up to 18000 hectares, the farmer here cannot on dry land where he do some sheep farming , he cannot be economical.

VO: 8”
The ANC has assured us they will take that into account. But they are set on limiting title deeds to 2 farms. George says it’s a blow.

George:
The problem with that is we have water allocations to some of those title deeds and if we lose some it means the others are not viable or not suitable at all for farming.

Bennie:
There’s a lot of farms at this stage that has perhaps 15 title deed and then only at that stage an economical unit, so if you cut that person down to only two he will go out of production.

VO: 14”
During SONA President Zuma also announced that foreigners would no longer be able to own agricultural land. It came as a shock to Zimbabwean farmer Zane Gilchrest who was thrown out in 2003 and has now resettled in South Africa.

Zane:
I’m a bit nervous because I am still a Zimbabwean. And then we call it a farm, but I’ve bought three units to make up one unit and now the new law says I am only allowed two title deeds where I am sitting now with three, so ja it’s worrying. I really don’t want to go through it again, to start again. It’s easy to fall, but to start.

VO: 4
We’ll need to see if it stands up to constitutional muster.

Gwede:
When that comes into law it must be applied retrospectively, but we will have to test it, whether constitutionally it can pass the test.

VO: 7
These proposed sweeping changes will have a huge impact on the profitability of commercial farms and the rural economy.

George:
Farmer’s doesn’t know what to do, they don’t know whether they should expand, whether they should put effort in.

Bennie:
People are very angry because they don’t have land, my question back to them is what are you going to do if the people don’t have food?

VO: 18”
Food prices have increased by on average 6% year on year. The biggest increases according to statistics are chicken at 19% and milk at 18%.
If we erode our farming base any further we’ll go from being a net exporter of food to being a net importer. And that’s a precarious position for any country to be in because you are at the mercy of fluctuating currencies and market vagaries.

George:
There’s going to be a food shortage, there is going to be people who are not going to have food to eat and its going to make the prices of food go through the roof, Inflation on food will go that people will not be able to afford food.

George: There’s going to be a food shortage, there is going to be people who are not going to have food to eat and its going to make the prices of food go through the roof, Inflation on food will go that people will not be able to afford food.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Malema says the land must be taken and Zuma must pay - we look at how the emotional proposals around land will impact on our food security.
metadata.Summary: It seems whenever politicians want to win votes the land issue rears its head. Its a cheap shot at winning votes. EFF leader Julius Malema has been very vocal on the issue and it seems it has not gone unnoticed by the ruling party. President Zuma at the recent lekgothla promised to ramp up land expropriation and it appears his remarks have sent jitters through the agricultural sector. Landbou.com have 13000 farms for sale and commercial farmers have dwindled from 67 000 in 1990 to 33 000 currently. These are the same farmers who provide around 95% of our locally produced food.
metadata.Further information: Commercial agriculture is worried. The land expropriation bill calls for no more than 2 title deeds and land not bigger than 12000 hectares. Given that this is a numbers game that relies on economies of scale a farm in the Western Cape cannot be compared to a farm in the Karoo for instance and organised agriculture says the plans are poorly thought out and unviable. Couple this with calls from government for farmers to hand over 50% of their farms to their workers in BEE deals and its easy to see why our food security is in danger. And if that is not enough - if we don't get rain in the next 10 days Grain SA warns our crops for the season will be dismal. We ask how do we keep our food basket full given all these dynamics?
